rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable role — a software developer or engineering team lead at a company running multi-ecosystem mobile/backend projects — who has demonstrated budget intent by explicitly preferring a paid hosted option. Willingness to pay is moderate: adjacent paid tools (Snyk, Dependabot, Renovate) exist but none aggregate multi-ecosystem deprecation data via machine-readable feed in exactly this way. The critical blocker is buildability: ingesting live deprecation signals from npm, Maven, CocoaPods, and SPM registries, normalizing breaking-change metadata, and reliably serving a REST/RSS API requires substantial data-pipeline work well beyond Claude prompts and a landing page — this is a data-infrastructure product, not a wrapper service. Operational autonomy is also limited because the data pipelines need ongoing maintenance as registry formats shift. Build gate fails on both `buildability_with_ai` (4 < 6) and `operational_autonomy` (5 < 7).
solution_plan: This is a multi-ecosystem library deprecation and breaking-change tracker delivered as a REST API and RSS feed. Building it properly requires scheduled scrapers against npm, Maven Central, CocoaPods, and SPM registries — that's real backend infrastructure that the Claude factory cannot assemble alone without a developer. A lightweight version (npm-only, Claude-extracted changelog summaries, simple API) could be validated: the factory can build a landing page with a Stripe payment link, an intake form asking which ecosystems and libraries to track, and a Claude prompt that parses changelogs on a schedule. Outreach would go to developer communities on Lobste.rs, Hacker News, and dev-focused newsletters — the factory drafts and queues the outreach for Youval's approval before anything sends. Ongoing delivery would be semi-automated: Claude processes changelogs, formats the feed, and emails subscribers, but Youval would need to approve any new integrations and monitor for registry format changes. Realistically, a solo non-technical operator cannot build the full multi-ecosystem version; the npm-only MVP is feasible for validation but the full product as specified requires engineering work.
notes: Fails build_gates: buildability_with_ai=4 (min 6), operational_autonomy=5 (min 7). Validate with an npm-only MVP to test willingness to pay before committing to the full data-pipeline build.
